Adversarial review: Larkspur Ferries funding pack (draft 3)
Read as a sceptical assessor would. Mark each row in the last column once checked.
No.QTopicHow a sceptical reader would attack thisWhat the pack already says in defenceGap / exposureSuggested fixSeverityCheck
1Q12Passenger forecast basis“You forecast 410,000 passengers in year two, yet the only evidence is one summer survey of 300 people at a single pier. Why should anyone believe the winter numbers?”Q12 cites the 2023 pier survey and a regional tourism growth figure of 4%.No winter data, no sensitivity range and no comparison with a similar route elsewhere.Add a low, central and high case, state the winter assumption plainly and cite one comparable route with its actual figures.High
2Q56 vs Q16/Q49Fleet cost inconsistency“Q56 says two vessels cost 9.2m in total, Q16 budgets 8.1m and Q49 mentions a third hull. Which is it, and does the board know the figures disagree?”Q56 gives the supplier quote; Q16 was written before the quote arrived.Three answers give three different totals, which reads as a pack nobody checked end to end.Pick the supplier quote as the single source, correct Q16 and Q49 to match it, and add one table reconciling all fleet costs.Critical
3Q7Safety certification“You say certification is in hand, but name no certifying body, no date and no fallback if the inspection fails. In hand could mean anything.”Q7 states that the operator holds a current licence for its existing route.The new vessels need their own certification and the pack is silent on timing.Name the certifying body, give the booked inspection window and say what happens to the launch date if it slips.Critical
4Q23Fare affordability claim“A 6.50 single fare is called affordable for commuters, with no reference to local wages or to what the bus costs for the same journey.”Q23 compares the fare with the tourist cruise price of 14.00.The comparison is with a leisure product, not with the commuter alternative.Compare the fare with the bus and rail price for the same journey and with median local hourly pay.Medium
5Q31Staffing plan“Forty-two crew are needed by launch and you currently employ nine. Where do thirty-three qualified crew come from in a region with a known shortage?”Q31 describes a training partnership with the harbour college.The college course takes eighteen months and launch is in eleven.Show the recruitment pipeline by month, including agency cover for the gap, and its cost.High
6Q40/Q41Environmental benefit“The carbon saving assumes every passenger would otherwise drive alone. That is the most flattering assumption available and you have not defended it.”Q40 uses the national average car emissions figure.No evidence on what passengers actually do today; the saving could be half the stated figure.Use the survey's own travel-mode split, and present the saving as a range with the method in an annex.Medium
7Q18Match funding status“Is the 2.4m match funding committed or merely hoped for? The wording moves between secured, expected and in discussion across three pages.”Q18 lists the funders and amounts in a table.Only one of the three funders has signed; the table does not say so.Add a status column to the funders table with the date of each signed letter, and use one word consistently.Critical
8Q9Governance and oversight“The project board meets quarterly. On a build this size that means a problem can run for three months before anyone senior hears of it.”Q9 names the board members and their experience.No description of what is reported between meetings or who can stop spending.Describe the monthly report, the escalation route and the spending limit above which the board must approve.Medium
9Q62Terminal lease“Your whole timetable depends on a terminal you do not own, on a lease that ends two years before the loan does.”Q62 notes a good relationship with the port authority.A good relationship is not an option to renew; the lease end date is absent from the risk register.Seek a written option to renew, add the lease to the risk register and state the fallback pier.High
10Q3Benefit to residents“The summary promises jobs for local people but the pack never defines local or commits to a number.”Q3 estimates 60 jobs in total across the operation.No definition, no target and no way to check afterwards.Define local by postcode area, commit to a share of roles and say how it will be reported each year.Medium
